routes.description: Move from an assumed fundamental reality to God-like perfection by treating unexplained nonmaximal parameters as arbitrary and reducing such arbitrariness across perfection-relevant attributes.
routes.successCriteria: Establish that relevant foundational limits require explanation, that the foundation possesses greatness or value, and that unresolved limits cannot remain in its perfection-relevant attributes.

motionBridge.description: Connect the absence of arbitrary limits in foundational greatness, power, positivity, and persistence to a perfect or quasi-perfect foundation.

centralBridges.description: Supply a defensible reason why apparently arbitrary foundational limits require further explanation.
Establish that fundamental reality possesses some greatness or value to which limits reasoning can apply.
Show that explaining a limited attribute cannot merely relocate the same arbitrariness into a deeper necessitating ground.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Specify how unexplained parameters count in comparative theory choice even when the argument is not independently conclusive.
Preserve a moderated conclusion by requiring arbitrariness to be reduced as far as the available explanations permit.

routes.description: Block the move to God-like perfection by showing that explanatory principles, foundational value, and the inference from explained limits to maximal attributes require independent comparative support.
routes.successCriteria: Show that rival theories may rationally retain explained or brute limits, that greatness or mentality is not established, or that nonarbitrariness does not entail maximal perfection.

motionBridge.description: Establish that the limits argument does not by itself discriminate decisively between a perfect foundation and relevant non-theistic or imperfect foundations.

centralBridges.description: Require assessment of unexplained limits within an all-things-considered comparison of competing theories and their virtues.
Challenge the premise that fundamental reality has value, greatness, or mentality sufficient for the perfection inference.
Preserve the possibility of a necessary or essential explanation for a nonmaximal foundational attribute.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Distinguish unexplainedness, inexplicability, and the relevant modal alternatives within the concept of arbitrariness.
Test whether the support for explaining limits equally supports rival principles with contrary theoretical consequences.

sections.title: Arbitrariness and the argument's comparative scope
sections.rationale: This issue fixes the operative concept of an arbitrary limit and determines whether the argument purports to demonstrate its conclusion or identify a comparative theoretical cost.

sections.title: Support for explaining fundamental limits
sections.rationale: The route from bounded foundational attributes toward an unlimited foundation depends on whether apparent irrelevant differences and explanatory practice justify extending explanation to the fundamental case.

sections.title: Foundational greatness and mentality
sections.rationale: Limits reasoning reaches perfection only if fundamental reality has a perfection-relevant degree of greatness or value, and its reach toward theism also depends on the separate issue of mentality.

sections.title: Grounding value in the foundation
sections.rationale: This issue determines whether derivative valuable states warrant attributing value to their ultimate ground, which supplies a required premise for applying limits reasoning to greatness.

sections.title: Explained submaximal limits and inherited arbitrariness
sections.rationale: The decisive transition from nonarbitrariness to perfection turns on whether a submaximal limit can be explained without transferring unresolved arbitrariness into its deeper ground.
